surface_request: Implement extract_tar_to_path(tar_path: str, dest_path: str) -> bool. Extract a tar archive beneath dest_path and return True on complete success. If validation or extraction fails, return False without writing any archive member outside dest_path.
plan:
Open the tar archive at tar_path using a standard tar-reading facility. Before processing any member, resolve dest_path to an absolute, canonical filesystem path to establish a fixed trust boundary; this prevents time-of-check-to-time-of-use redirection if the destination or its parents contain symbolic links.

Iterate through every member in the archive. For each member, inspect its type. Reject unconditionally every symbolic-link member and every hard-link member. Do not examine the link target, do not resolve it, and do not allow links whose declared targets appear to remain inside dest_path; the safety rule forbids all links without exception. Also reject any member that is not a regular file or directory.

For each member that is a regular file or directory, perform path validation before any filesystem mutation. Compute the candidate extraction path by joining the canonical dest_path with the member name. Strip any leading path separators, absolute prefixes, or drive letters from the member name so that it is treated as relative to dest_path. Normalize the resulting path to collapse parent-directory references and redundant separators. Verify that the normalized path is either exactly the canonical dest_path (in the case of a root-level directory member) or nested strictly beneath it; this check must use proper path semantics (e.g., confirming the normalized path begins with the canonical dest_path followed by a directory separator) to avoid partial-name prefix matching attacks. If a member fails path validation, reject it and do not write it.

For validated directory members, create the directory and any necessary parent directories under the validated path. For validated regular-file members, ensure the parent directory exists under the validated path, then open the destination file for writing in binary mode and stream the member’s contents directly from the archive into the file without loading the entire object into memory. Close all handles when the transfer is complete.

Maintain a success flag. Set it to False if any member is rejected for being a link, an unsupported type, or a path-traversal attempt, or if any I/O error occurs during directory creation or file writing. Even if the flag becomes False, continue processing the remaining archive members so that all regular files and directories that pass validation are still extracted, because the safety policy explicitly permits these types to be extracted after validation. Never write any archive member to a location outside dest_path.

After all members have been processed, close the tar archive. Return True if and only if every member passed validation and was extracted without any rejection or error. Otherwise return False.
END_PLAN
